; Disable every APU channel, clear driver masks and reset all five stream pointers to $88AB. The pointed
; idle stream is bank-local.
; Initialize all five channel cursors; X counts down from four.
; A selects a track. Form 5*A and load five low/high stream pointers. For track values below 64,
; the two ASLs clear carry before ADC. Initialize each channel through a
; zero event and schedule its first decode on the next tick.
; Split pointer tables use a shared index: one entry for each of five channels per track.
; Process a pending effect when the request sign bit is set, then decrement five channel delays. Only a
; delay reaching zero advances its stream. The enabled-mask sign bit instead requests global silence.
; The low five bits select channels; bit 7 changes the tick into a silence request.
; Each stream has an independent byte countdown.
; Continue through pulse 1, pulse 2, triangle, noise and DMC.
; Return to the banked caller.
; Stop hardware output while leaving stream cursors intact.
; X selects a channel; clear its bit in both sounding and enabled masks.
; X selects a channel. Copy its saved cursor to zero page and consume commands until a timed event or a
; stop path returns. Timed events below $80 contain [value, delay_minus_one]; value zero uses the preset
; mute masks. Delay $FF wraps to zero and will wait 256 ticks.
; Negative bytes are command tokens; nonnegative bytes are timed events.
; Save the cursor after both bytes of the timed event.
; FE consumes one preset index and immediately continues decoding.
; FF reloads the track/channel restart cursor from the alternate split pointer tables and immediately
; decodes it. This is a restart, not an inline address.
; FC resets the current stream to $88AB before sharing the FB stop path.
; FB takes the channel stop path without replacing its saved cursor.
; If sounding, clear channel masks unless every channel is enabled, then apply a zero event. Keep a one-
; tick delay. This path does not save the current zero-page cursor.
; A zero event combines the selected preset with channel-specific mute masks.
; Return with a one-tick countdown; subsequent behavior depends on the saved stream cursor.
; E2 stores its following byte minus one in the shared parameter. Its later game meaning remains unresolved.
; Any other negative command silences the driver and forces X to four, ending the outer tick loop.
; Advance past the command argument and continue decoding within this tick.
; Increment the 16-bit stream cursor, preserving X and Y.
; Cursor increment is complete.
; A is event value and X is channel 0..4. Ignore disabled channels. Select a four-byte APU preset; value
; zero applies per-channel mute masks. Pulse/triangle pitches use period lookup tables plus a
; track/channel adjustment; noise and DMC copy preset register bytes directly. Restore X and clear Y
; before returning.
; Nonzero events preserve the preset control byte and mark this channel sounding.
; DMC is first disabled before replacing its register values.
; Split tables select a four-byte preset. Multiply channel index by four to address its APU register quartet.
; Skip register writes for a disabled channel.
; Copy preset bytes two and three, then reconcile the DMC enable bit with the sounding mask.
; Pulse event values subtract twelve before period-table indexing.
; Noise copies preset timer bytes; DMC uses its separate enable sequence. Other channels use the pitch tables.
; Index the period tables with event plus the track/channel adjustment. Merge the high period byte with
; preset byte three.
; Restore the channel index for the caller and reset Y for the next stream read.
; Noise takes preset bytes two and three directly; there is no pitched period lookup.
; Use two split pointer entries per effect. Nonzero high bytes replace channel 1 and channel 3 streams,
; reset their delays and optionally enable their APU bits. Clear the request after installation. Effect
; names and priority policy remain unknown.
; The second effect stream targets channel 3; a zero high pointer skips that stream.
; Consume the pending effect request even if both pointers were absent.

; Load the resource directory pointer from $8004/5. Its first byte is the stride between
; parallel scene-parameter arrays; start at 1+SceneSetupParameter, then read low/high pointer
; components from successive strides. High bytes in the first directory are relative to $8000;
; the second directory at $A004 supplies graphics pointers relative to $A000 and raw descriptor
; pointers. Calls build mutable five-byte scene records and four-byte markers. Finally take the
; composite table span from its leading byte and advance the pointer past that header.
; Carry is explicitly cleared only at the shown entry points: directory sizes/relative offsets
; are assumed to fit the intended byte arithmetic. Effective PRG pair [4,5] is required.
; Build the five-byte records from the selected stream and type/value tables, preserving the directory cursor.
; Build the marker list from the selected three-byte stream, preserving the directory cursor.
; Read the second directory at CPU $A004, using $A0-relative high bytes for graphics pointers.
; The leading count separates parallel low/high composite-pointer arrays. Advance the base by one byte.
; Resource pointers and mutable lists are now ready for their consumers.
; Preserve the directory cursor on the stack. Read [column flags,row,type] triples until a $FF
; column sentinel. Expand each into a five-byte record with state bit $10, type-table contact value,
; and timer. Timer descriptor byte type*5+1 equal to $FF stays $FF; otherwise choose a scrambler
; value 1..16. Scene $11 additionally sets column bit 7 for type one. Set full-list and visible-list
; byte bounds, with first visible offset zero. Stream bounds rely on the sentinel.
; X advances by five destination bytes; Y advances by three stream bytes.
; Store either the $FF sentinel or the selected 1..16 initial timer.
; Restore the source cursor after table lookups and advance to the next triple.
; Publish byte bounds and restore the resource-directory cursor.
; Read [tile X,tile Y,flags] triples until tile X $FF. Expand each to four bytes with phase $FF,
; store the byte end offset, and restore the resource-directory cursor. No sentinel is copied.
; Initialize one marker and advance source by three, destination by four.
; Publish the marker-list byte bound.
; Count actors whose state high nibble matches the shared target. Return carry set only when
; contact/gate bits $70 are all clear, allowing normal actor dispatch. Otherwise return carry clear
; while clearing individual delay gates when their conditions expire: bit $10 uses $02F8; bit $40
; uses actor tile Y plus four against BackgroundLogicalRow; bit $20 uses tile Y minus $21.
; The final test still uses the original saved flag byte, so cleared bits may remain in this local copy.
; Save the original contact flags before testing the three update-delay gates.
; A nonzero shared busy byte keeps bit $10 set.
; Clear the shared-busy delay bit when its condition has ended. If neither row gate remains, continue
; into the actor category/direction update; otherwise preserve the remaining gate bits for the row
; tests.
; Convert actor Y to a byte tile row by shifting its word right three.
; Use unsigned byte subtraction and comparison for the second row gate.
; Carry clear tells the fixed caller to skip its normal actor-state path.
; Choose the actor category from the fixed type descriptor. With descriptor bit seven clear use bits
; four/five; otherwise shift its low nibble into the category high nibble. Quantize the direction from
; the actor position to the scene reference, restore the current actor offset, then install that
; direction and reset motion fractions/contact timer.
; For the alternate descriptor form, the low nibble becomes the actor category high nibble.
; Carry set permits the fixed actor-state path.
; Copy view X low into the scroll shadow. Split view Y into its tile row and low three pixel
; bits; publish the logical tile row, reduce a copy modulo thirty, then recombine its pixel offset
; for the hardware Y-scroll shadow.
; Reduce the temporary tile row modulo thirty.
; Multiply the wrapped tile row by eight and restore the sub-tile pixel offset.
; Destructively subtract scene-reference coordinates from the two input words at $BE..$C1 and
; take their unsigned magnitudes. Return max(abs X,abs Y)+floor(min(abs X,abs Y)/2) in $38/39.
; The comparison determines which magnitude to halve; this is a cheap distance estimate.
; Normalize the second coordinate difference after the first magnitude is ready.
; Compare the absolute words to decide which contributes at half weight.
; The first magnitude is at least the second.
; Add the full larger magnitude and halved smaller magnitude as a word.
; Build a five-byte render record only when the actor lies within the view window and the 40-byte sort
; list has room. Actor state high nibble plus ActorTypeBase selects the image family and coordinate
; flags. Contact flag bit two chooses a compact image form; otherwise category/direction selects the
; directional image. Publish sort key three for category zero, eleven otherwise, and retain the actor
; coordinates in the record.
; Combine the actor direction low nibble with the category offset table and this type/state image-
; family base.
; Reserve a two-byte sort entry; carry set means the global 20-record limit is full. On success use
; its render-record offset to store actor coordinates and image. The X high byte retains bits
; seven/zero and merges the type descriptor low-nibble coordinate flags.
; Clear contact flag bit seven, then test actor minus view coordinates. The high-byte tests admit a
; small negative margin by adding $20 with the subtraction carry; positive Y additionally requires low
; byte below $F0. A visible actor regains flag bit seven and returns carry set; an excluded actor
; returns carry clear. Scratch $38/$39 is destructive; X remains the actor offset.
; Apply the same signed high-byte window check to Y; a nonnegative row then also tests the $F0 lower
; edge.
; Mark the actor visible to the render pass and return carry set.
; Keep the cleared visibility flag and return carry clear.
; This bank API is a no-op return.
; Attempt the actor type's reference-directed object action only when its extension/cooldown byte is
; zero and state is neither five nor six. Reject negative type descriptors. Category mismatch is
; allowed only when the alternate fixed descriptor low nibble is nonzero. Measure max(abs(dx),abs(dy))
; plus half the smaller distance to the scene reference, and continue only below 150 pixels. The type
; descriptor selects the object allocation type; exact game roles vary by actor.
; Use the shared return helper to restore the current actor index.
; The bank-local type index addresses the fixed descriptor tables.
; Prepare the two coordinate words for the destructive distance estimate.
; Reject an unsigned approximate reference distance of 150 or greater. This is a 16-bit comparison, so
; nonzero high distance bytes also reject.
; Combine scene category and actor direction to select paired signed pixel offsets. Add each signed
; byte to its actor coordinate word with sign extension and carry, producing the new object position
; in the allocator workspace. Save actor direction as the object contact parameter and scene category
; as its category.
; Install the type-specific actor cooldown before attempting allocation, so capacity rejection still
; consumes the cooldown. Clear object contact flags and call the fixed typed-object allocator with the
; saved action type. Carry set skips the sound request; success requests effect nine. Both exits
; restore the dispatcher's current actor X.
; Restore X from the fixed dispatcher saved actor offset.
; Two signed byte-coordinate offset arrays with 24 entries each, consumed as paired X/Y samples. Their
; direction-dependent numeric symmetry and separate read bases establish the two-plane layout; exact
; actor/graphic assignments are unresolved.
; Preserve caller Y and sample a signed coordinate offset selected by actor category and direction.
; Convert the resulting actor pixel position to tile coordinates, wrapping X to nine bits, and query
; the fixed tile classifier. Retain the maximum class, then invoke this bank's $802A hook with A=1.
; Carry set from the hook ends sampling; otherwise the count initialized to one is decremented, with
; another offset plane selected if the hook extended it. Restore Y and return carry set exactly when
; the maximum class exceeds the actor category. Hook-specific scene effects remain described at that
; bank's hook.
; Add the signed first-coordinate offset, with high-byte correction.
; Prepare the second coordinate high byte and signed offset.
; Add the second offset, with high-byte correction.
; Shift both sample words right three for the fixed tile-class query.
; Keep the unsigned maximum tile class in scratch. The following A=1 load does not change carry: an
; RTS-only hook therefore stops immediately when this comparison was greater or equal.
; Call the bank-specific tile hook. On carry clear, select the next 24-entry offset plane, restore
; current actor X and decrement the remaining sample count; repeat only while nonzero.
; Restore caller Y and compare category high nibble against the maximum sampled class. Return carry
; set when category is smaller, carry clear otherwise; A retains the category.
; Two signed byte-coordinate offset arrays with 24 entries each, consumed as paired X/Y samples. Their
; direction-dependent numeric symmetry and separate read bases establish the two-plane layout; exact
; actor/graphic assignments are unresolved.
; Scale the unsigned byte adjustment in A according to scene-counter low nibble three through ten.
; Subtract three to select eight local handlers, and expand the input to a 16-bit value times eight.
; The dispatcher itself has no range clamp. The handlers return the original input or a rounded
; fraction; scratch input, term, total and indirect pointer are destroyed.
; Return one of the unsigned input in A. This identity handler bypasses accumulation and rounding.
; Return seven eighths of the unsigned input in A. Compose the fraction by halving the expanded term
; and accumulating selected terms, then round the total before returning.
; Return thirteen sixteenths of the unsigned input in A. Compose the fraction by halving the expanded term
; and accumulating selected terms, then round the total before returning.
; Return three quarters of the unsigned input in A. Compose the fraction by halving the expanded term
; and accumulating selected terms, then round the total before returning.
; Return five eighths of the unsigned input in A. Compose the fraction by halving the expanded term
; and accumulating selected terms, then round the total before returning.
; Return one half of the unsigned input in A. Compose the fraction by halving the expanded term and
; accumulating selected terms, then round the total before returning.
; Return seven sixteenths of the unsigned input in A. Compose the fraction by halving the expanded
; term and accumulating selected terms, then round the total before returning.
; Return three eighths of the unsigned input in A. Compose the fraction by halving the expanded term
; and accumulating selected terms, then round the total before returning.
; Add eight to the 16-bit total, then shift right four and return its low byte in A. This rounds the
; fractional scale to nearest integer, with halves rounded upward; the high total byte is consumed by
; the shifts.
; Divide the unsigned 16-bit term by two in place; return its new low byte in A.
; Initialize the 16-bit accumulator from the current term.
; Add the current 16-bit term to the accumulator, preserving carry between bytes.
; Interleaved little-endian CPU handler pointers selected by the adjacent bounded dispatcher. The
; index is the validated counter low nibble three through ten, minus three; eight entries select
; scene-adjustment arithmetic. Pointer values describe CPU views, not physical storage identities;
; bank context remains required.
; Run this bank-specific special-actor update only for scene index two.
; Other scenes return immediately.
; A nonzero feedback timer consumes this update: decrement it and queue the palette-feedback step.
; Otherwise dispatch the special actor state: zero returns, seven runs the exit-particle path, and
; other active states tick the actor/object spawn timers.
; State zero is inactive; seven has an additional helper before the common update.
; Update the active special actor's actor-spawn and object-spawn timers.
; Return after the state-dependent calls.
; While the audio-channel gate is nonzero, give each update a one-in-eight chance to append an object
; of type $90 if the 14-record object list has room. Choose X from $E0 plus a masked random byte and Y
; from $58 plus another, load this type's contact descriptor, set phase three and choose its contact
; mode with carry set. Advance the object end by eleven bytes. A zero gate deactivates the special
; actor instead; the gameplay reason for coupling this path to that gate remains uncertain.
; Clear the full special actor state byte when the shared channel gate is zero.
; For states other than ten, decrement a nonzero actor-spawn timer or attempt a spawn when zero.
; Independently decrement the object timer or attempt its phase-gated object spawn when zero. State
; ten uses the object timer as a defeat delay; expiry changes only the state low nibble to seven and
; reloads the delay to $80, which is decremented on this update.
; After the state-ten delay expires, preserve state high bits, enter state seven and load $80 into the
; shared object/phase timer before its common decrement.
; Allow at most two 13-byte actor records. Choose one of four coordinate pairs, clear motion
; fractions/contact timer/extension, initialize state one with phase timer $14, contact flags $0C and
; auxiliary byte ten, then aim the new actor toward the scene reference. Combine the direction with
